title: Geometry - Lesson 6 Practice: Indirect Measurement
description: Practice using shadows, mirrors, and scale drawings to solve indirect measurement problems with similar figures.

questions.question: A 1.5 m student casts a 2 m shadow. At the same time, a pole casts an 8 m shadow. How tall is the pole?
questions.explanation: Use corresponding ratios: 1.5/2 = x/8. Then 2x = 12, so x = 6 m.

questions.question: In a mirror problem, a person's eye height is 1.6 m, the person is 2 m from the mirror, and a tree is 10 m from the mirror. Which proportion can find the tree height x?
questions.explanation: Eye height corresponds to object height, and person-to-mirror distance corresponds to object-to-mirror distance, so 1.6/2 = x/10.

questions.question: A scale drawing uses 1 cm to represent 4 m. A hallway is 6 cm long on the drawing. What is the real hallway length?
questions.explanation: Each centimeter represents 4 m, so 6 x 4 = 24 m.

questions.question: When two objects cast shadows at the same time on level ground, their height-shadow triangles can be treated as similar triangles.
questions.explanation: The objects are vertical, the ground is horizontal, and the sun angle is the same, so the right triangles are similar.

questions.question: In a mirror sightline problem, the two ground distances should always be added before writing the proportion.
questions.explanation: Each triangle uses its own distance to the mirror. Adding the distances usually breaks the corresponding-side relationship.

questions.question: Convert 150 cm to meters before using it in a meter-based proportion.
A 2 m pole casts a 3 m shadow. A tower casts a 15 m shadow at the same time. The tower is ___ m tall.
questions.explanation: Use 2/3 = x/15. Then 3x = 30, so x = 10 m.

questions.question: Explain why unit consistency matters when setting up an indirect measurement proportion.
questions.correctAnswer: Units must be consistent so the ratios compare like measurements. For example, heights should both be in meters or both be in centimeters before solving.
questions.explanation: A proportion compares corresponding quantities. Mixing meters and centimeters without converting changes the ratio and can produce a wrong answer.
